CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFAUTHENTICATE

CFAUTHENTICATE checks a user name and password against the user directories of a security context. On success the user counts as authenticated for the rest of the request (and, with the default cookie, for later requests), so IsAuthenticated, AuthenticatedUser and IsAuthorized can answer questions about them.

Category

Security

Syntax

<CFAUTHENTICATE SECURITYCONTEXT="context"
    USERNAME="user_ID"
    PASSWORD="password"
    SETCOOKIE="Yes/No"
    THROWONFAILURE="Yes/No">

Attributes

SECURITYCONTEXT
Required. A security context defined on the Advanced Security pages of the Administrator.
USERNAME
Required. The user's ID in one of the context's user directories.
PASSWORD
Required. The user's password.
SETCOOKIE
Optional, default "Yes". Yes sends the cookie CFAUTHORIZATION_context, which keeps the user logged in on later requests. With No, the login lasts for the current request only.
THROWONFAILURE
Optional, default "Yes". Yes throws an exception of TYPE="Security" when the user name or password is wrong. With No, check IsAuthenticated() or the variable CFAUTHENTICATE.AuthenticationStatus ("Success" or "Failure") instead.

Usage

If the security context does not exist, CFAUTHENTICATE always throws a Security exception, whatever THROWONFAILURE says. Catch it with CFCATCH TYPE="Security".

The usual place for the tag is Application.cfm: if IsAuthenticated() returns No, show a login form; when the form comes back, call CFAUTHENTICATE with the submitted values. Afterwards AuthenticatedUser() and AuthenticatedContext() return the user and context, and IsAuthorized() checks the context's rules and policies.

The authorization cookie carries the user, the context and a scrambled (not encrypted) password, which is checked again on every request; changing a user's password logs them out. Use SSL if the network between you and your users is not to be trusted.

KoldFusion keeps user directories, contexts, rules and policies in its own registry, managed on the Advanced Security pages of the Administrator. The tag works whenever the named context exists.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFPARAM NAME="Form.UserName" DEFAULT="guest">
<CFPARAM NAME="Form.Password" DEFAULT="guest">

<CFOUTPUT>
<FORM ACTION="cfauthenticate.cfm" METHOD="POST">
User: <INPUT TYPE="Text" NAME="UserName" VALUE="#HTMLEditFormat(Form.UserName)#" SIZE="12">
Password: <INPUT TYPE="Password" NAME="Password" SIZE="12">
<INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Log in">
</FORM>
</CFOUTPUT>

<!--- The "Snippets" context exists only if an administrator created it --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFAUTHENTICATE SECURITYCONTEXT="Snippets" USERNAME="#Form.UserName#"
      PASSWORD="#Form.Password#" SETCOOKIE="No">
  <CFOUTPUT><P>Welcome, <B>#AuthenticatedUser()#</B>!
  You are logged in to the context #AuthenticatedContext()#.</CFOUTPUT>
<CFCATCH TYPE="Security">
  <CFOUTPUT><P><B>Not logged in:</B> #CFCATCH.Message#<BR>
  <I>#CFCATCH.Detail#</I></CFOUTPUT>
</CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>

<CFOUTPUT><P>IsAuthenticated() returns #IsAuthenticated()#.</CFOUTPUT>
